title: Credit Issued to Put a Billing Error Right on a Granite Ridge Pass Account
content:
Credit issued to put a billing error right on a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme pass account is held back from the amount drawn in an application, because money credited to correct a charge is returned rather than recycled against what is owed.

**First.** Where the pass account shows credit issued to put a billing error right and the pass record still admits the holder, the whole of that error credit is held back.

**Second.** Where the pass account shows credit issued to put a billing error right and the pass record does not admit the holder, half of that error credit is held back, a share of 50 per cent of it.

**Otherwise.** In any other case nothing is held back on this account.

### What is held back

| Credit issued to put a billing error right | The pass record | Amount held back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| standing on the pass account | still admits the holder | the whole of that error credit |
| standing on the pass account | does not admit the holder | half of that error credit |
| none standing | either | nothing on this account |

The figure held back answers only to the entries issued to put a billing error right; credit issued for any other reason is not held back on this account. The amount held back is deducted from the rounded figure the share drawn produces, not from the pot.

### Worked on a hypothetical account

A pass account showing 90.00 of credit issued to put a billing error right, on a record that still admits the holder. The whole 90.00 is held back, so a drawn figure of 300.00 is brought down by 90.00 at this step.

On the same account with the record no longer admitting the holder, half of 90.00 is held back, which is 45.00, and the drawn figure is brought down by 45.00 instead.
